title: Backpressure

validation.research: Seven primary references: Reactive Streams 1.0.4 specifies demand-bounded delivery and non-pausable sources; Node.js documents normal writable admission/readiness, pipeline coordination, threshold versus total memory and independent transform buffers; Flink establishes the spaced spelling Back Pressure and output-buffer constraints propagating upstream; Kafka 4.1 documents buffer blocking limits and additional memory; Python closing, synchronization and task documentation establish the actual ownership, suspension and cooperative cancellation behavior. Backpressure is capacity feedback, not a fixed rate quota or durable processing acknowledgment. A normal writable backpressure false can follow an accepted chunk, so it must not trigger resubmission; error/closure also require handling because drain may never arrive. Original 5000/2000/6000 rates, export, stream processor and retained-log 180000/90-second cases remain. Code, event-gated experiment and native illustrations are original teaching material.

runnable_example.verification: Actual article fences run unchanged on Python 3.11+. A real Event holds the first write while repeated event-loop turns leave source reads at one and completed bytes at zero; release resumes the three sequential writes with peak one unfinished callback, six bytes and a closed source. Empty input, zero-length chunks, order/counts and caller-owned destination lifetime are verified. A callback with gated finally cleanup keeps the next source read blocked until its TemporaryFile closes. Exact source/sink errors preserve prior completed effects, stop further reads and close actual source/callback files. Cancellation during the second write closes owned files without reversing the first write or reading the third chunk. Pre-start cancellation leaves the source caller-owned and explicitly closed by the caller. All created tasks are awaited and no background task remains. Original steady-rate calculations match 6000 places in two seconds, 180000 backlog in sixty seconds and ninety-second net drain. No total-memory bound, real database/file transfer, deadline, worker pool, retry, durable acknowledgment, remote cancellation or reversal is inferred.

example_limits: Existing data-backpressure is revised in place, preserving canonical ID/URL/title/summary, Data Engineering tags/verse and allocation asset path, original 5000/2000/6000 steady-rate arithmetic, CSV/compression export, Flink slow-sink diagnosis, retained-log backlog 180000 and net-drain 90-second calculation, Kafka bounded blocking caveat and historical import metadata. Back Pressure is a spaced spelling, not a different pattern. The one primary home moves to Reliability and Failure Handling; Streaming & event processing keeps a cross-link and thirteen other members. Original article/SVG archived locally. Original Python 3.11+ transfer owns a closeable incremental synchronous generator once its coroutine starts, awaits each asynchronous writer before requesting the next item and counts only completed callbacks. The generator must advance without blocking I/O and produce bounded chunks; callback work/cleanup must finish before return, without detached operations. A real Event gates the first writer while source-read count remains one and completed bytes remain zero. Three chunks of lengths 1/2/3 finish with six bytes and a closed source after owned release/join. The caller owns destination lifetime and pre-start source cleanup. No worker pool, per-chunk task queue, hard total-memory bound, deadline, timed rate limiter, durable acknowledgment, retries, deduplication or remote rollback is supplied. Tests verify real suspension, zero read-ahead during the held write and its cleanup, peak one unfinished callback, resume/order/counts, empty input, zero-length chunks, exact source/sink errors, real TemporaryFile closure, cancellation after ownership starts and caller-owned pre-start cleanup. Prior completed writes remain visible. All created tasks are awaited. The events model a controlled writer; no actual network/database transfer, complete memory bound, deadline, cancellation of remote work or durable business acknowledgment is inferred.
